title: Valid Sudoku
kidExplanation: A Sudoku page. Every row, every column, and every 3×3 box may show each digit at most once. Empty cells are fine.
plainProblem: Determine if a 9×9 board is valid Sudoku so far (not necessarily solvable). '.' means empty.

examples.input: board with one duplicate in a row

thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: For each filled cell, scan its row, column, and box.

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: Keep three families of hash sets: rows, cols, boxes.

thinkingSteps.title: Better idea
thinkingSteps.body: One pass: if a digit already sits in that row/col/box set, invalid; else add it.

pattern.name: Hash set / hash map for seen items
pattern.whenToSpot: You need fast lookups of values you already saw.

complexity.timeReason: The board is fixed 9×9, so work is constant (or O(n²) for an n×n generalization).
complexity.spaceReason: At most 9×9 entries across the sets for a standard board.

edgeCases: Duplicates and boundary values from the constraints.
commonMistakes: Coding before stating the pattern and complexity.
Off-by-one errors on indices or window edges.
Mutating data structures while iterating carelessly.
interviewTips: Name the pattern: Hash set / hash map for seen items.
State O(1) time and O(1) space at the end.

steps.caption: Start solving valid sudoku using the hash view.
Walk the main loop. Watch the highlighted piece — yellow means 'looking now'.
Finish. Green means done. Compare with the expected LeetCode example.

interviewApproachNotes: Hash sets per row/col/box is the clear interview solution. Mention the box index formula out loud.
